newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-BURKE RECALLED BY WALLABIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BURKE RECALLED BY WALLABIES.

text.p: Australia fullback Matthew Burke has gained an immediate recall for the second test against France at Ballymore on Saturday after recovering from a groin injury.
Australia coach Greg Smith named Burke as the only change to the side who beat beat the Five Nations champions 29-15 in the first test on Saturday.
The Wallabies' regular goal-kicker came in for Stephen Larkham, the Australian Rugby Union said on Monday. Larkham joins the replacements.
Burke's return means reserve winger Mitch Hardy is likely to lose his seat on the bench at Ballymore despite scoring the two tries that lifted Australia to victory in the first test.
Hardy, called into the squad at late notice as cover when Burke pulled out, made a stunning impact on his international debut.
During an eventful 12-minute stint as a temporary replacement while Larkham underwent treatment for a facial injury, Hardy scored twice to break a 15-15 deadlock.
Wallaby number eight Daniel Manu was named in the starting line-up but he faces a fitness test on a shoulder injury later in the week. Veteran forward Troy Coker was put on stand-by.
France play the Australian Barbarians in a tour match in Newcastle, New South Wales, on Tuesday.

Australia - 15-Matt Burke; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson, 6-Brett Robinson, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-David Giffen, 3-Ewen McKenzie, 2-Marco Caputo, 1-Richard Harry.
